Title: Enzymes in the Human Body
Subtitle: How Biological Catalysts Speed Up Life Processes
Body:
Enzymes are special proteins in the human body that act as biological catalysts, meaning they speed up chemical reactions without being used up themselves, and they are essential for life because they help control processes such as digestion, energy production, and cell repair; each enzyme is highly specific, meaning it only works with a particular substance called a substrate, fitting together like a lock and key at the active site, and once the reaction occurs the enzyme releases the product and can be used again, and examples include amylase in saliva which breaks down starch into sugars, protease enzymes in the stomach which break down proteins, and lipase which breaks down fats, and because enzymes work best under specific temperature and pH conditions, changes in the body environment can affect how well they function, which is why maintaining homeostasis is important for healthy biological activity.
